spec.text: Why is the South-West Monsoon called ‘Purvaiya’ (easterly) in Bhojpur Region? How has this directional seasonal wind system influenced the cultural ethos of the region?

scenes.vo: UPSC, twenty twenty-three. General Studies Paper One, ten marks, one hundred and fifty words. Why is the South-West Monsoon called Purvaiya, easterly, in the Bhojpur region? And how has this wind system influenced the region's culture? Here's the puzzle. A south-west monsoon with an east wind's name.

spec.text: Why is the South-West Monsoon called ‘Purvaiya’ (easterly) in Bhojpur Region? How has this directional seasonal wind system influenced the cultural ethos of the region?

scenes.vo: Read what it asks. Why asks for a cause. How has it influenced asks for effects. So there are two jobs. The reason for the name. And the mark it left on culture.

lines.text: In Bhojpuri song, purva is the easterly wind.
A song collected in Jaunpur reads, gusts of easterly winds blow.

scenes.vo: Start with the word. In Bhojpuri song, purva is the easterly wind. A song collected in Jaunpur reads, gusts of easterly winds blow.

lines.text: Then the Bay of Bengal branch meets the Arakan Hills.
It bends, and runs west up the Ganga plain.
So it arrives from the east.

scenes.vo: But the monsoon is south-west. Yes, over the sea. Then the Bay of Bengal branch meets the Arakan Hills. It bends, and runs west up the Ganga plain. So it arrives from the east.

lines.text: Its monsoon trough runs from Ganganagar through Prayagraj to Kolkata.
North of that line, winds are easterly or south-easterly.
Placing Bhojpur there is our own step.

scenes.vo: IMD gives the weather map. Its monsoon trough runs from Ganganagar through Prayagraj to Kolkata. North of that line, winds are easterly or south-easterly. Placing Bhojpur there is our own step. IMD never names it, so say it with care.

lines.text: The rains set the farm calendar.
Paddy sowing runs from the third week of June to the fourth week of July.
A Jaunpur work song says, it's raining, let's go transplant paddy.

scenes.vo: Now the culture. The rains set the farm calendar. Paddy sowing runs from the third week of June to the fourth week of July. A Jaunpur work song says, it's raining, let's go transplant paddy.

blocks.text: _Purvaiya_ is the easterly (_purva_) wind of Bhojpuri song; the monsoon's Bay branch reaches the Ganga plain from the east.
1. Why easterly

• The Bay of Bengal branch, bent by the Arakan Hills, moves _westward_ along the Ganga plain (NCERT). • IMD: north of the _monsoon trough_ (Ganganagar-Prayagraj-Kolkata) winds are easterly or south-easterly; placing Bhojpur there is our inference.
A flow: the Bay branch, the Ganga plain, the Purva wind, the Kajari song.
blocks.label: Fig. 1: From the Bay of Bengal to the song

items.what: Sawan songs of rain and parting

blocks.text: 2. Cultural ethos

• _Farming_: paddy is sown from the third week of June, and rain calls transplanting in song (Jassal). • _Kajari_, sung by women in Sawan (July-August); the slack season brings visits to natal homes. • _Migration_ shaped Biraha, Bidesiya and Kajari: the same wind pains wives left behind (Chauhan and Mishra). • 50,579,447 speak Bhojpuri (Census 2011).
So the easterly sets the work, the songs and the ache: a boon for fields, a pain for the parted.

scenes.vo: Now we write. One hundred and fifty words, about seven minutes. Open by translating the word. Purva means easterly. Then the Bay branch.

weak.text: Purvaiya comes from a Bhojpuri suffix meaning 'from'.
weak.miss: no scholarly source gives that etymology; the word appears in songs as the easterly wind

weak.text: A south-west monsoon cannot be easterly.
weak.miss: north of the trough, winds are easterly or south-easterly

weak.text: IMD names Bhojpur's wind as easterly.
weak.miss: IMD names the trough, not Bhojpur: that step is our inference

weak.text: Festivals like Hariyali Teej come from the easterly wind.
weak.miss: no official or university-press source ties them to it
the songs also call it an enemy of wives left behind

scenes.vo: Now the easy answer beside it. It invents an origin for the word, from a suffix. It says a south-west monsoon cannot be easterly. It credits festivals to the wind with no source. It says the wind only brings joy. And it says IMD named the Bhojpur wind. It did not.
